top.line: A forensic look at why a release takes about 24 minutes, and why a second run should do no work.

in-short.line: 16.7 minutes local, 1.4 gate, 6.3 CI; CI steady; half the local time a borrowed generator run three times.
in-short.para: Keep the checks; stop redoing work.

question.line: The quality control lets agents release ten times a day; the question is where 24 minutes go.

ci.line: 437 CI runs and 327 releases since 18 October; median 5.3 to 5.9 minutes a week since 21 October.
ci.para: Failures cluster in the reader tests.

local.line: Two timed releases: sgit.ai's generator 12.6 minutes, run three times at about 173 seconds each; tests 212 seconds.
local.para: A collage redraw may force a third run.

twice.line: Tests, the meter test, validation, the sitemap and the cards are done twice or more on the same tree.

second-run.line: Load, extract, transform, save: hash inputs, sign and commit manifests, rebuild only deltas, full run daily.
second-run.para: The change is itself a check.

recommendations.line: Six steps: unchanged work, the failing first run, tests once per tree, parallel steps, LETS, an own generator.

limits.line: Two timed runs; CI duration method; the collage lead; October figures from the earlier piece.

sources.line: Timed release runs, the gate's timing, a month of GitHub Actions runs, and the build code.
